page.layout: One page of text, verse set in lines with no columns and no margin notes. Running head at top centre, page number at top right. Signature mark at the foot right.

p.i: Quæ nescit almi Numinis leges sacras Coliique stulta Dæmones.
O quanta nostris ira fumat naribus: Ignesque quantos excitat.
Ut sæva fervet ore nostro funditus Quæ flamma terras concoquit.
Ut alta torrens antra, campos frugibus Lætoque priuat gramine.
Ut ultima[?] montium fundamina Basesque firmas subruit.
O quanta pœna gentis impiæ manet Rebelliones perfidas.
Illius ecce congeram in dirum caput Cunctas cohortes cladium.
Fortique tela cuncta torquens brachio. Illam seuerus obteram.
Uret cruenta marcidam fames, simul Ardens caterua febrium.
Uagam per arua cuncta dente fervido Fera vorabunt obuia.
Languebit atque fracta duris cladibus Sæuisque sub malis gemet,
Serpentiumque fauciata morsibus, Et nigra tabo corruet.
Illius atque bella finibus ferent Hostes cruenta barbari.
Si forte firmis exit urbibus foras

page.notes: Printed letters: the scan shows long-s and f-like forms; all are read as plain s. Ligatures "ct" and "ti" are written out. The word "ultima" in line 10 is doubtful: the scan reads "vrit ima", so it is marked [?]. The word in line 17, "seuerus", has an f-like initial that could be read as sæ-; it is given as printed-looking "seuerus". The v/u spelling is normalised by rule: consonant v in fervido, obuia, vorabunt, urbibus is written v, vowel u initially in Uret, Uagam. Lines are verse; each sentence is written as one paragraph with line ends joined by spaces. Paragraph breaks follow the sentence ends as printed.
